criterion: A refused publish shows its reason beside the poster in question, naming the missing written alternative.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the message sits next to the poster in the studio editor and says the written alternative is missing. No if the message appears only as a page-level banner, or if the missing field is unnamed.

criterion: The refusal a signed-up account meets at the studio reads as a deliberate decision rather than as something going wrong.
evaluation_rule: Yes if that reader is returned to a working public surface that says in the house's own voice that the studio is not theirs. No if the refusal reads as an error, a dead end, or a half-drawn studio the reader is left standing in.

criterion: On the studio palette each record shows its own state in words beside its title.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each row states whether the record is live or held back, in words. No if the state is carried by a colour, an icon or a position alone.

criterion: The page that follows a publish reads as an ending rather than as another form.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the confirmation is composed in the house's own register and offers one onward move. No if it is a bare success screen, or if it puts the publish control back in front of a producer who has just used it.

criterion: The studio's first screen presents the palette as the way work is done rather than as one control among a page of chrome.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a producer arriving at the studio can see that typing is the next thing to do. No if the palette shares the screen with a toolbar, a sidebar or a dashboard that competes with it for the first move.

criterion: The studio's create route belongs to the same house as the public site rather than reading as an admin form bolted on behind that site.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the create route carries the site's own frame, type and restraint. No if it is set in a default form style, or if its chrome is unrelated to the chrome a visitor sees.

criterion: A drained still on the public work index reads as a deliberate treatment rather than as a picture still arriving.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the resting index reads as a composed page of colourless photographs. No if a drained still is indistinguishable from a placeholder, a broken image or a loading state.

criterion: On the entry cluster, the work index and the roster alike the two grounds read as a matched warm pair rather than as black on white.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the dark surface reads as warmed toward red and the pale one as warmed toward green, and the site never reads as neutral grey. No if the pair reads as pure black and pure white, or as two unrelated temperatures.

criterion: The roster reads as one composed screen in which the name, the label, the mark and the portrait belong to a single figure.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the four elements sit as one arrangement under the name. No if they read as four stacked blocks, or if the name has to share the screen's weight with anything around it.

criterion: A link on a public route is recognisable as a link by a reader whose pointer stays parked.
evaluation_rule: Yes if position, setting and grouping make what is pressable legible at rest. No if finding what is pressable requires sweeping the pointer, or if a colour is what marks it.

criterion: The about route's blur reads as attached to the reader's hand rather than as an effect played at them.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the sharpening tracks the wheel continuously and stops where the reader stops. No if it advances in steps, runs ahead of the scroll, or leaves text unreadable once the reader has stopped moving.

criterion: Under a reduced-motion preference the about route still reads as the designed page rather than as a stripped fallback.
evaluation_rule: Yes if that reader loses the effect and nothing else, with the same blocks in the same places. No if the route drops content, shifts its layout, or reads as a plain unstyled version of itself.

criterion: The focus ring is legible on the pale ground, on the dark ground and over a photograph alike.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a keyboard reader can find the focused control on all three surfaces. No if the ring disappears against one of them, or if it reads as a browser default dropped onto a considered page.

criterion: The narrow roster reads as the same roster a wide window shows rather than as a different page.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the name setting, the order and the sense of one talent at a time all survive the change. No if the narrow layout reads as a list, a grid or a stack that the wide layout never suggested.

criterion: A visitor on a phone is shown the work as a colour portfolio, with nothing held behind a gesture that device cannot perform.
evaluation_rule: Yes if everything a pointer would reveal is already present on the narrow layout. No if a caption, a colour or a title is reachable only by a hover on a surface that has no pointer.

criterion: The fade between two public routes reads as unhurried rather than as the site being slow.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the change reads as one object turning a page. No if the reader is left waiting on a dimmed screen, or if the fade is indistinguishable from a slow response.

criterion: A commissioner can tell from any public route how to reach the house, and finds one address rather than a form.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the enquiry channel is findable from the chrome on every route and resolves to the house's own address. No if it is buried on one route only, or if the site asks the reader to fill in fields instead.

criterion: An emptied roster speaks in the house's own register rather than as a system message.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the sentence reads as written by the house and does not read as a failure. No if it reads as an error string, a placeholder, or a developer's stub.

criterion: A work index caught mid-load looks like the work index rather than like a page being assembled.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the reserved spaces read as part of the composition, carrying no spinner, no shimmer and no dimensions drawn across them. No if the loading page shows skeleton furniture the finished page never has.

criterion: The dependency manifest names Flask with its Jinja template layer, Alpine.js, a PostgreSQL driver and a production WSGI server and nothing beside them; no second datastore client, cache client, queue client, object-store SDK, search library, mail library or identity-provider SDK is declared.
evaluation_rule: A dependency is a package named in a manifest's runtime dependency block -- the Python requirements or project file, and the front-end package manifest -- not a transitive lock entry and not a development-only tool such as a formatter, a linter or a test runner. Yes if every runtime dependency is Flask, its bundled Jinja template layer, Alpine.js, a PostgreSQL driver, a production WSGI server, or a direct requirement of one of those five. No if the manifest names a second datastore client beside the one addressed by DATABASE_URL, a cache client, a queue or task-runner client, an object-store SDK, a search-index library, a mail or SMTP library, an identity-provider or session-vendor SDK, an image or video transform client, or any package that no obligation in this brief reaches.

criterion: No module in the tree implements a capability the checklist never asked for: there is no cart, price or payment code, no comment, like, share, rating or view-counter store, no site-search index, no newsletter or mail sender, no chat widget and no second analytics library.
evaluation_rule: A capability is implemented when the tree carries source for it -- a route, a table or migration, a model, a Jinja template, an Alpine component or a request handler -- whether or not anything links to it. Yes if the only capabilities present are ones the brief names: the entry cluster, the works index, the work detail, the roster and its discipline filter, the talent detail, about, signup, studio login, the preview harness, the studio palette with its create, edit, publish, unlist and reorder paths, the JSON API under /api, GET /api/health and the seed. No if the tree carries a cart, a price field or a payment path, a comment, like, share, rating or view-counter table, a site-search index or a search endpoint, a newsletter list or any routine that sends mail, a chat widget, or a second analytics library beyond the single page-view counter; note that the CONTACT label opening a mail composition to the house's contact_email, the footer's INSTAGRAM and LINKEDIN labels, and the generated og:image share card are named by the brief and are none of these.

criterion: Every file in the tree is reached from a route table, a model, a template, a settings module or the seed module that a checklist obligation required; no framework scaffolding and no unreferenced helper survives unused.
evaluation_rule: A file is reached when an import chain starting at the Flask application module names it, when a handler renders it through the template loader or another reached template extends or includes it, when it is the settings module read at startup, or when it is the seed module run at boot. The deployment artifacts the brief demands -- /app/USER_README.md, the empty .browser_screenshots/ and .downloads/ directories, and the container and manifest files -- are outside this judgement. Yes if every remaining module and every Jinja template in the tree is reached by one of those paths. No if the tree holds a generated framework scaffold that no route table names, a helper module nothing imports, a second copy of a module kept beside the live one, a template no handler renders and no template extends, an unused blueprint registered nowhere, or a commented-out route left behind after a rewrite.

criterion: No binary file is committed anywhere in the tree - no image, no moving-image file, no typeface file and no icon file - and every generated artwork routine derives its output in source from the seed stored on the record it belongs to.
evaluation_rule: A binary file is any committed file whose bytes are not source text -- a raster or vector image file, a moving-image file, a typeface file or an icon file -- settled by the file's extension and by whether the tree stores it as readable text. Generated artwork means the four routines the brief names: the still generator, the reel generator, the 300px grain tile and the 1200 x 630 share image. Yes if no such binary file exists anywhere in the tree, with every mark written as inline vector geometry in the Jinja markup and the display and interface faces named and loaded rather than shipped, and if the still routine in source reads the seed column of the media row it draws for, choosing two of #313236, #676767, #333333, #455e53 and #dedede and its angle from that seed, with the reel routine taking its displacement direction from the same stored seed. No if the tree commits a .png, .jpg, .webp, .svg, .mp4, .webm, .woff2, .ttf, .otf or .ico file, if the share image or the grain tile is committed as a file rather than produced by a routine in source, if a drawing routine calls an unseeded random source or the clock so two requests for the same media_id could differ, or if the still routine draws text, its own dimensions or a diagonal cross.

criterion: One naming scheme governs the whole tree: module names, model names, template file names and the context keys handed to those templates follow a single convention rather than one convention per surface.
evaluation_rule: A naming convention is the casing and separator style a name uses -- snake_case, kebab-case, camelCase or PascalCase -- judged across four surfaces: module file names, model class names, Jinja template file names, and the context keys handed to render calls. Yes if each surface holds one convention throughout and the context keys match the model attribute names they carry, so a template receiving an items row reads the same key names the model declares, such as house_id, published_at and talent_item_id. No if two module files in the same package use different separator styles, if one template is named work_detail.html beside another named work-detail.html or workDetail.html, if a context key is selectedWork in one render call and selected_work in another, if a model class named Item sits beside one named media_row, or if the same concept is a talent in one module and a name the brief never uses -- an artist, a member, a profile -- in another.

criterion: The house-scoping decision is written once as one reusable unit of source that every studio read path and every studio write path applies, rather than restated inline in each handler.
evaluation_rule: The house-scoping decision is the rule that a record whose house_id is not the caller's house_id is answered exactly as a record that does not exist, so the answer never confirms the record is real. One reusable unit of source means one named function, query helper, decorator or base query carrying both the house_id comparison and the not-found answer. Yes if that single unit exists and every studio path calls it: GET /api/studio/items, GET /api/studio/items/{id}, POST /api/studio/items, PATCH /api/studio/items/{id}, the publish and unlist path, POST /api/studio/items/{id}/media, POST /api/studio/items/{id}/credits, POST /api/studio/items/{id}/slug, POST /api/studio/works/order, POST /api/studio/preview-tokens and the token resolution at GET /api/preview/{token}. No if any handler writes its own house_id comparison inline, if one handler scopes by house while a sibling loads the record by id alone, if the reorder or token-minting path is scoped differently from the read path, or if one path answers a foreign record as forbidden while another answers it as not found, so the two answers together disclose that a cirrus record exists to a meridian producer.

criterion: The four derived values - the read-time ordinal, the discipline set, a talent's selected work and a work's neighbours - are each computed by one helper the whole tree calls, and none of the four is also held as a stored column.
evaluation_rule: The four derived values are exactly the ones the brief names: the read-time ordinal, contiguous from 001 and zero padded to three digits; the discipline set in first appearance order; a talent's selected work read from credits; and a work's neighbours, wrapping 012 to 001. One helper means one named function that every caller -- Jinja template, JSON serialiser and studio handler alike -- routes through. Yes if each of the four has exactly one such function and the items schema carries none of the four as a column. No if the ordinal is zero padded inside a template while a serialiser pads it again for GET /api/works, if the discipline set is authored anywhere as a literal list of director, photographer and stylist beside the derived computation that publishing Noor Vasquez must extend, if a talent row carries a selected-work column instead of reading credits, if neighbours are computed inline in the /works/{slug} handler and again in GET /api/works/{slug}, or if items declares an ordinal, number, next_id or previous_id column beside its stored position.

criterion: The thirty-two character lowercase hexadecimal identifier that media rows and preview tokens both carry is minted by a single helper every model calls, so the convention has one definition in source rather than a repeated literal per table.
evaluation_rule: The identifier is the 32 character lowercase hexadecimal value that media.id and preview_tokens.token both carry, and a single helper means one named minting function that every model and the seed call. Yes if exactly one function in the tree produces that value and it is the only source of media.id at POST /api/studio/items/{id}/media, of preview_tokens.token at POST /api/studio/preview-tokens, and of both when the seed writes the poster rows for The Quiet Room and Noor Vasquez. No if one table's value is minted by one call and the other's by a different call, if the length 32 or a hex alphabet appears as a literal in more than one module, if one path lowercases its output while another accepts whatever case the underlying call returns, or if the seed module writes its own hex identifiers instead of calling the same helper.

criterion: Instants are held in UTC and a slug is lowercased at one boundary before it is stored or compared, and both conventions are applied identically in every model, seed routine and serialiser that touches them.
evaluation_rule: An instant is any value stored in a timestamp column -- created_at on houses, accounts, items, media, credits' parent rows, preview_tokens and slug_redirects, published_at on items, and expires_at on preview_tokens -- and the slug boundary is the single point at which a slug string is lowercased before it is stored in items.slug or slug_redirects.old_slug or compared against either. Yes if every instant is produced by one UTC-aware source, the columns are declared to hold UTC, and one named function lowercases a slug and is called by the create path, the rename at POST /api/studio/items/{id}/slug, the redirect row it writes, the public lookups and the seed. No if any module calls a naive local-time now, if the 15 minute expires_at is computed from a different clock than the created_at written beside it, if GET /api/works/{slug} or GET /api/talents/{slug} compares the request path segment against the stored slug without passing it through that function so Rives and rives resolve differently, if a handler calls its own lowercasing expression inline instead of the shared function, or if the seed module lowercases its slugs with an expression of its own.
